math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
weighting the parts that are most relevant
math_plain: Re-weight importance of facets (genre, character, pacing) based on user interaction signals to reorder search results.
why_math: Users clarify intent through subtle actions; weighting facets by feedback adapts the ranking to match each person's evolving goals, making results more relevant than a one-size-fits-all score.

math_tags: measuring similarity as nearness in a space
math_plain: Index scenes, objects, faces, and speech as points in space so searching means finding nearby points in that space.
why_math: When you represent different modalities (images, audio, text) as positions in the same space, similarity naturally becomes distance: closer things are more alike, and distance queries become fast lookups.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
separating cause from coincidence
math_plain: Score patents by disruptive potential and evolution using network citation patterns and clustering to surface high-impact technologies.
why_math: Citation networks reveal which patents influence others; grouping patents by topic shows where breakthroughs cluster. Combining these separates genuinely transformative work from one-off contributions.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
smart random sampling and averaging
math_plain: Pool many small vector scores across a page into summary scores at coarser tile scale, then rerank using full detail.
why_math: You only need the rough order for candidate generation, not exact scores; averaging coarser patches gives that order fast. Only the top candidates need exact rescoring, so the two-stage approach cuts work quadratically.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
learning a function from examples
math_plain: Rank and combine retrieved passages by learned scores to feed most relevant sources into response generation.
why_math: Learned ranking assigns higher scores to passages that actually help models generate correct answers. Reranking before generation lets the model focus on gold-signal facts rather than processing all possibilities.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
measuring similarity as nearness in a space
math_plain: Score and rank Nepali documents against queries using learned embeddings that capture morphological structure.
why_math: Words with similar roots should place near each other in embedding space; learnable scoring of that nearness ranks relevant documents highest despite morphological variation in the language.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
math_plain: Rerank and expand queries using large models to improve search for low-resource languages (Hausa, Fongbe).
why_math: Large models encode multilingual knowledge even for rare languages; reranking candidates with learned scores from that knowledge surface relevant results despite sparse training data for the language itself.

math_tags: combining many weak signals into a strong one
weighting the parts that are most relevant
math_plain: Score and fuse query classification outputs from the same model prompted in three languages, weighting by confidence.
why_math: A single language may misclassify due to ambiguity; prompting in typologically different languages surfaces different signal strengths. Confidence-weighted fusion combines these signals so strong votes outweigh weak ones.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
learning a function from examples
math_plain: Score and rank retrieval results to feed relevant schema snippets into models that map natural language to SQL.
why_math: Models make fewer mistakes when shown similar past queries and schemas; ranking retrieval results by relevance puts gold examples first, improving in-context learning and reducing hallucinated SQL.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
math_plain: Benchmark systems that score and rank agricultural answers for drought-prone Telugu-speaking farmers.
why_math: A standardized ranking benchmark with human judgments lets researchers measure whether scoring functions improve real-world information access for farmers without benchmarks, enabling fair comparison of methods.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
math_plain: Score web results retrieved by LLMs to measure accuracy of Marathi information retrieval, analyzing search depth effects.
why_math: Scored rankings reveal whether shallow or deep search ranks correct answers highest; measuring score distributions exposes failure modes and cost-accuracy tradeoffs, guiding deployment strategy.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
spreading information across a network
math_plain: Rank sentences using learned embeddings plus graph message-passing over discourse structure to select for summarization.
why_math: Sentences interact via discourse (earlier sentences set context for later ones); spreading information through that graph captures which sentences are central to meaning. Ranking by this network-aware score selects faithful summaries.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
separating cause from coincidence
math_plain: Score text patterns to distinguish LLM-generated agricultural answers from human-authored ones.
why_math: LLMs produce consistent patterns (length, diversity, similarity) that differ from human text; scoring and classification separate true signal from noise, revealing detectability as a diagnostic for evaluating generated content.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
weighting the parts that are most relevant
math_plain: Score and rank in-domain examples from translation memory and glossaries to weight LLM post-editing and improve machine translation.
why_math: Domain-specific terminology matters most; ranking retrieved examples by relevance to current phrase and weighting their influence over the baseline translation focuses the model on high-confidence domain knowledge.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
measuring similarity as nearness in a space
math_plain: Score and rank Shona documents by learning embeddings that preserve morphological relationships to improve retrieval.
why_math: Morphologically related words should score as similar; learning that structure places documents with related word forms near the query in embedding space, retrieval by proximity then ranks them highest.
